title: dot11decrypt_util: Avoid abusing memory layout
description:
Instead of using a single memcpy which relies
upon struct members being in contiguous
memory, use three separate calls to memcpy.

This fixes Coverity 1460754.

notes.body:
Given that the addresses are 6 octets long, the compiler will probably inline the `memcpy()`s anyway, and will probably optimize further so that the code generated will be the same anyway if the structure members are contiguous (which they probably will be).

So we might as well go for more correct code.

> the code generated will be the same anyway if the structure members are contiguous

Not with Apple clang version 11.0.3 (clang-1103.0.32.62), either with -O2 or -Os:

```
$ cat copyrama.c
#include <string.h>

#define DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN 6

struct frobozz {
	unsigned int a;
	unsigned char addr1[DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN];
	unsigned char addr2[DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN];
	unsigned char addr3[DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN];
};
	
void
docopy(unsigned char *buf, struct frobozz *p, unsigned char b)
{
	buf[0] = b;
	buf[1] = b + 17;
	memcpy(buf + 2, (unsigned char *)p->addr1, DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN);
	memcpy(buf + 8, (unsigned char *)p->addr2, DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN);
	memcpy(buf + 14, (unsigned char *)p->addr3, DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN);
}				
	
void
docopy2(unsigned char *buf, struct frobozz *p, unsigned char b)
{
	buf[0] = b;
	buf[1] = b + 17;
	memcpy(buf + 2, (unsigned char *)p->addr1, 3 * DOT11DECRYPT_MAC_LEN);
}				
$ cc -S -Os -Wall -W copyrama.c
l$ cat copyrama.s
	.section	__TEXT,__text,regular,pure_instructions
	.build_version macos, 10, 15	sdk_version 10, 15, 6
	.globl	_docopy                 ## -- Begin function docopy
_docopy:                                ## @docopy
	.cfi_startproc
## %bb.0:
	pushq	%rbp
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
	.cfi_offset %rbp, -16
	movq	%rsp, %rbp
	.cfi_def_cfa_register %rbp
	movb	%dl, (%rdi)
	addb	$17, %dl
	movb	%dl, 1(%rdi)
	movzwl	8(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 6(%rdi)
	movl	4(%rsi), %eax
	movl	%eax, 2(%rdi)
	movl	10(%rsi), %eax
	movl	%eax, 8(%rdi)
	movzwl	14(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 12(%rdi)
	movl	16(%rsi), %eax
	movl	%eax, 14(%rdi)
	movzwl	20(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 18(%rdi)
	popq	%rbp
	retq
	.cfi_endproc
                                        ## -- End function
	.globl	_docopy2                ## -- Begin function docopy2
_docopy2:                               ## @docopy2
	.cfi_startproc
## %bb.0:
	pushq	%rbp
	.cfi_def_cfa_offset 16
	.cfi_offset %rbp, -16
	movq	%rsp, %rbp
	.cfi_def_cfa_register %rbp
	movb	%dl, (%rdi)
	addb	$17, %dl
	movb	%dl, 1(%rdi)
	movq	4(%rsi), %rax
	movq	12(%rsi), %rcx
	movq	%rax, 2(%rdi)
	movq	%rcx, 10(%rdi)
	movzwl	20(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 18(%rdi)
	popq	%rbp
	retq
	.cfi_endproc
                                        ## -- End function

.subsections_via_symbols
```

and gcc (Ubuntu 9.3.0-17ubuntu1~20.04) 9.3.0 does the same:

```
ubu20-04$ gcc -S -O2 -Wall -W copyrama.c
ubu20-04$ cat copyrama.s
	.file	"copyrama.c"
	.text
	.p2align 4
	.globl	docopy
	.type	docopy, @function
docopy:
.LFB11:
	.cfi_startproc
	endbr64
	movb	%dl, (%rdi)
	addl	$17, %edx
	movb	%dl, 1(%rdi)
	movl	4(%rsi), %eax
	movl	%eax, 2(%rdi)
	movzwl	8(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 6(%rdi)
	movl	10(%rsi), %eax
	movl	%eax, 8(%rdi)
	movzwl	14(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 12(%rdi)
	movl	16(%rsi), %eax
	movl	%eax, 14(%rdi)
	movzwl	20(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 18(%rdi)
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
.LFE11:
	.size	docopy, .-docopy
	.p2align 4
	.globl	docopy2
	.type	docopy2, @function
docopy2:
.LFB12:
	.cfi_startproc
	endbr64
	movb	%dl, (%rdi)
	addl	$17, %edx
	movb	%dl, 1(%rdi)
	movdqu	4(%rsi), %xmm0
	movups	%xmm0, 2(%rdi)
	movzwl	20(%rsi), %eax
	movw	%ax, 18(%rdi)
	ret
	.cfi_endproc
.LFE12:
	.size	docopy2, .-docopy2
	.ident	"GCC: (Ubuntu 9.3.0-17ubuntu1~20.04) 9.3.0"
	.section	.note.GNU-stack,"",@progbits
	.section	.note.gnu.property,"a"
	.align 8
	.long	 1f - 0f
	.long	 4f - 1f
	.long	 5
0:
	.string	 "GNU"
1:
	.align 8
	.long	 0xc0000002
	.long	 3f - 2f
2:
	.long	 0x3
3:
	.align 8
4:
```

Perhaps there's something about the C language semantics of `memcpy()` and of structures that requires this, or maybe neither Clang+LLVM nor GCC is optimizing vigorously enough.

But that's probably not pessimal enough to make it worth the hack (unless profiling of decryption shows otherwise).
